Kay Lee Continues Her Journey For Justice At Florida Prison
– What One Person Can Do

See
Jeb Bush Is About to Find Out the Hard Way That He Has Met His Match In Kay Lee,
As She Protests Abuse of Federal Marijuana Prisoner In State Prison.

August 20, 1999

Dear Compassionate Friends,

Grandma Kay Lee's Journey for Justice continues today. She left Melbourne FL this morning on the final leg of her venture. Today she will test the waters at Starke, get a feel for the atmosphere at the prison and check out her safe house.

Kay Lee has been writing prisoners for many years. Her current journey to the Florida Correctional Institute in Starke is a result of her 3 year correspondence with Gary Waid, an inmate at the Starke facility.

Gary has been eloquently detailing his experience as a POW on his web page. Continuing reports of violence by Guards and the total disregard for Human Rights has kept prison reform a high priority for compassionate people like Kay. The beating death of Starke prisoner, Frank Valdez, as a result of Guard Brutality prompted Kay to act.

Kay began systematically getting the word out about the conditions at Starke. In letters to the Governor, the Warden and finally, in a plea to the press (to get citizens involved), she has called for real investigations into the conditions at Starke. The atmosphere of concern has empowered 13 other inmates to come forward with their own accounts of the routine beatings administered by guards. Kay will be at the

facility at Starke, meeting with other prisoners families and holding vigil until a list of demands are met. "I wish we could do this for the whole country...(make the prison walls transparent)", Kay said in a late night meeting with her support team.

In Melbourne, Kay and her support team made plans to assure her safety and effectiveness. Kevin Aplin and Scott Bledsoe, of the Cannabis Action Network, will assist Kay as she presents her demands to the Warden this week. Supporters will join Kay as she meets with families on Saturday August 21, 1999. CAN attorneys stand ready to advise Kay should the need arise.

Kay will continue to send her reports from the front as she can. For timely information, call 407-253-3673 as I will function as "air support".

Watch for regular updates and support Grandma Lee by joining her at Starke or sending contributions if you can't. Our prison population has surpassed the million mark, America houses a fourth of the worlds prison population. The continuing WAR creates more POW's everyday. Those of us who still enjoy a semblance of freedom must act now to negotiate an end to the WAR and protect the prisoners it has created.

With hope for the future......

Jodi James

Melbourne, FL

-----------------------------------------------------

August 19, 1999 9:00pm

Grandma Lee Arrives in Starke

Prison Put on Notice

Grandma Kay Lee and members of the Cannabis Action Network arrived at Starke Prison this afternoon. The crew drove proudly through the main gates of the prison in the famous Gainesville Hemp Mobile. Kay said they filled the lobby as they met with prison officials. Warden Crosby, however, was unavailable to meet with Kay.

"We've put them on notice, and we have them scrambling" stated a tired Kay Lee this evening. "Gary knows I'm here, his lawyer and family got a message to him." that is the important part to Kay, that the prisoners and their family know she is there. She is anxious for visiting hours on Saturday and a chance to hear the families stories.

Kay has taken up residence at a local motel and when asked about her future plans, she said she will be there until she has to go. Kay is a tower of resolve on the issue of creating "transparent prison walls".

Kay asked that the number at the motel be published to all lists. She is hopeful that people will contact her about joining the vigil. Kay will be limited in her internet access, but can be reached by phone.

For more information contact Kevin Aplin @ 352-378-9836 or Kay Lee @ 904-964-7357 room 103.

More as it becomes available.

Jodi James

Melbourne, FL
